A judge who strives to the best of his knowledge gets a double reward if his verdict is right and still a reward if it is wrong.
Umar wanted a witness for an instruction Abu Musa cited, which market business had hidden from him; Abu Huraira, staying close to the Prophet, narrated much and forgot nothing.
Jabir swore that Ibn Sayyad was the Dajjal, because Umar had sworn so before the Prophet and the Prophet did not object.
Horses bring reward if kept for Allah's Cause, shelter if kept for a living, and sin if kept for pride; for donkeys the Prophet cited only the atom's-weight verse.
A woman asked how to bathe after menstruation; the Prophet told her to clean herself with a perfumed cloth, and when she kept asking, Aisha took her aside and explained.
Mastigures were eaten on the Prophet's table cloth though he disliked them, so they were not unlawful; whoever eats garlic or onion should keep away from the mosque.
Asked by a woman what to do if she did not find him, the Prophet told her to go to Abu Bakr.
Ka'b reported truthfully about the People of the Scripture yet with faults; they are neither believed nor denied, and Muslims holding an undistorted Book should not ask them.
The Prophet said to recite the Quran while hearts agree on its meaning and to stop reading when people differ over it.
Near his death the Prophet offered to write something to keep them from going astray; Umar said Allah's Book suffices, the people disputed noisily, and he told them to leave.
Arriving for Hajj, the Prophet ordered the companions to end their ihram, making their wives lawful, saying he would too had he not brought the Hadi; they obeyed.
The Prophet said thrice to pray before Maghrib, adding the third time that whoever wants may do so, lest people take it as a Sunna.
When Aisha was slandered and revelation was delayed, the Prophet consulted Ali and Usama, questioned Barira, and asked from the pulpit for help against those abusing his wife.
Sending Mu'adh to Yemen, the Prophet told him to invite people first to Allah's Oneness, then prayer and Zakat; Allah's right on His slaves is worship of Him alone.
The surah 'He is Allah, the One' equals a third of the Quran, and a man who loved reciting it for describing the Beneficent was told Allah loves him.
Allah is not merciful to those who show no mercy; weeping over his dying grandson, the Prophet said this is mercy Allah puts in His slaves' hearts.
None is more patient than Allah with hurtful words: people ascribe children to Him, yet He gives them health and provision.
None but Allah knows the five keys of the unseen, and Aisha said whoever claims Muhammad saw his Lord or knew the unseen is lying.
Since Allah Himself is As-Salam, the Prophet told those praying not to say 'peace be on Allah' and taught them the tashahhud instead.
Allah will fold the heaven in His right hand saying 'I am the King'; the Prophet sought refuge in His Might; Hell fills when He puts His Foot on it.
The Prophet praised Allah at night as Lord, Light and Truth; he said Allah, Hearing and near, needs no shouting, and taught Abu Bakr an invocation for forgiveness.
Gabriel told the Prophet that Allah had heard what his people said and how they answered him.
The Prophet taught the istikhara: two voluntary rak'at, then asking Allah, who knows and is able, to ease a matter if good and turn it away if not.
The Prophet often swore by 'the One Who turns the hearts'.
Allah has ninety-nine Names, and whoever learns them all by heart will enter Paradise.
The Prophet taught invoking Allah's Name on going to bed, praising Him on waking, and a prayer before relations with one's wife so Satan never harms their child.
Game caught by trained dogs sent with Allah's Name may be eaten, as may meat brought by new Muslims when one mentions Allah's Name over it oneself.
The Prophet slaughtered two rams saying Allah's Name and Allahu Akbar; on the Day of Nahr he told anyone who slaughtered before the prayer to slaughter again.
Do not swear by your fathers; whoever swears should swear by Allah.
Of ten men the Prophet sent to scout the enemy, Khubaib was taken outside Mecca's sanctuary to be killed and recited verses on dying as a Muslim for Allah's sake.
None has more ghira than Allah, so He forbade shameful deeds, and none loves praise more than Allah.
When Allah created the creation He wrote about Himself in His Book, kept with Him on the Throne: 'My Mercy overcomes My Anger'.
Allah is as His slave thinks of Him and with him when he remembers Him, remembering him in return, and comes running to one who comes walking.
When the verse on torment from above and below came down, the Prophet sought refuge with Allah's Face, and called being split into parties easier.
Allah is not one-eyed, while the Dajjal, of whom every prophet warned, is blind in the right eye with 'Kafir' written between his eyes.
Asked about coitus interruptus with women captured in the battle with Bani Al-Mustaliq, the Prophet said it is better not to, for Allah has written whom He will create.
On Resurrection believers will seek intercession from Adam, Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus, then Muhammad, who intercedes again and again until those with an atom's weight of good leave Hell.
Allah's full Hand is undiminished by spending; He will grasp earth and heavens saying 'I am the King', as a Jew described with Fingers; and Allah has the most ghira.
The Prophet asked a man whether he knew anything of the Quran, and he named the surahs he knew.
Asked by Yemenis how the universe began, the Prophet said only Allah existed, His Throne over the water, then He created heavens and earth and wrote everything.
